newsitem.title: USA: Lock repair halts N. Illinois River barge traffic.
newsitem.headline: Lock repair halts N. Illinois River barge traffic.

text.p: Mechanical damage to the Peoria lock on the Illinois River halted all barge traffic north of the lock on Thursday at 1600 CST but the lock is expected to reopen Saturday at 2000 CST, Army Corps of Engineer officials said.
"The anchorage system on the lower land wall had started stripping the nut that holds the gate to the wall," said Mike Zerbonia, chief of maintenance for the Illinois Water Project Office in Peoria.
Zerbonia said a maintenance crew was on the way to Peoria and was expected to begin work by 2000 CST Friday.
The lock repair will require the use of a heavy crane to lift the more than 85-ton gate and should take 24 hours to complete, Zerbonia said.
Grain merchants in northern Illinois were expecting a very busy corn harvest day Friday and Saturday, and had hoped the lock would be working again by Saturday morning, they said.
